key_insight: NeuTNN-AV achieves competitive audio-visual classification using 4-bit spiking networks with far fewer synapses than leading SNN baselines.
engineering_relevance: Its comparison-and-addition inference supports resource-constrained multimodal sensing, though the abstract does not evaluate solid mechanics applications.
method: Encode inputs temporally, with each input line spiking at most once.
Use neurons with multiple active dendritic segments and local reward-modulated STDP learning.
Store weights as 4-bit integers and perform inference using only comparisons and additions.
evidence_signal: NeuTNN-AV reports 78.6% accuracy on CREMA-D with 2.34M synapses and 98.82% on UrbanSound8K-AV with 1.38M, plus 23–106× smaller weight memory than spiking baselines.
watch_item: Reported synaptic energy savings do not establish end-to-end system efficiency; preprocessing and hardware overhead require validation.
paper_title: HEAR, SEE, SPIKE ONCE: Highly Efficient NeuroAI Temporal Neural Networks for Low-Precision Multimodal Audio-Visual Classification and Online Learning
